title: SG-1.3 Rebuild GameLayout with Tailwind classes and the UI store
summary: GameLayout uses Tailwind utilities and useUiStore for an 80/20 desktop split and a mobile bottom drawer, with the legacy layout CSS removed
description: Context: game/frontend/src/components/GameLayout.tsx uses the legacy classes .game-layout, .scene-area and .story-panel from src/styles.css, plus a local useState drawer flag, although useUiStore already exposes drawerOpen and toggleDrawer. Desired behavior: on desktop the viewport shows an 80/20 game/story split with no page scroll or horizontal overflow. On mobile the story panel becomes a bottom drawer and the game controls stay reachable. Expected result: the legacy layout CSS is gone. Why: this is the responsive shell the StoryForge redesign requires.
acceptance_criteria: Given a viewport of at least 768px, when GameLayout renders, then the layout is a full-height grid with columns 4fr/1fr, the root has overflow-hidden, and the story aside scrolls on its own.
Given a viewport below 768px, when the Story toggle is clicked, then the aside moves from closed to open and the scene and its controls remain mounted and reachable.
Given src/styles.css, when it is read, then it contains no .game-layout, .story-panel or .scene-area rules and no @media (max-width: 768px) block.

in_scope: removal of legacy layout CSS from styles.css
updating tests that assert the legacy classes
preserve: Story toggle button named 'Story' with aria-expanded

technical_constraints: Button, Lucide ChevronUp and motion.aside stay in use
definition_of_done: Both requirements are implemented and verified by unit tests
non_functional: No horizontal overflow at any width
